ns2:section.sectionText: TOPICS IN QUANTUM OPTICS AND INFORMATION. The field of quantum information uses the nonclassical, often counter-intuitive, features of quantum physics (including the wave-particle duality, superposition, and entanglement) to surpass the information-processing capabilities of systems restricted by classical physics. We will first focus on experiments highlighting the underlying fundamental quantum phenomena, including tests of nonlocality, quantum erasers, the quantum Zeno effect, multi-particle interference, and fast- and slow-light. Building on this, we will then consider various topics in quantum communication, including quantum cryptography and teleportation, and some basic quantum information theory. Next we will survey the main quantum computation algorithms and techniques for error correction, concluding by discussing the main experimental "qubit" systems under investigation. There are ~8 problem sets, and 1.5 papers. Note: This course satisfies one of the Physics Department "breadth" requirements. Prerequisites: PHYS 580 is recommended. Advanced undergraduates admitted with consent of instructor.
